title: Expose issue close + abandon via deterministic CLI (cam issue close/abandon <id>)
description: closeIssueOnMain and abandonIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-specify.ts) already implement the deterministic commit-to-main mutation (stage:shipped / status:abandoned, guards + commit-tree on main) but are NOT wired to any CLI subcommand: cam issue only exposes create + list. So closing a subsumed/duplicate issue (hit live: CAM-192/198/180 subsumed by CAM-201) forces hand-editing the CAM-NNNN.json + a manual git commit, which the orchestrator should never do. Add thin dispatch wrappers cam issue close <id> and cam issue abandon <id> (mirroring cam issue --file-local): call the existing functions with a real spawnFn/clock, print a CAM_ISSUE_* result line, commit to main, exit non-zero on not-found/diverged. Concrete Layer-1 instance of the CAM-197 epic (deterministic CLI, zero LLM, function already exists). Origin: operator direction + hit live during CAM-201 post-merge housekeeping 2026-07-07.

spec.scope: Wire two new deterministic positional subcommands `cam issue close <id>` and `cam issue abandon <id>` into the CLI, mirroring the on-main pattern of `cam issue --file-local`/`list`. They call the ALREADY-EXISTING pure functions closeIssueOnMain / abandonIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-specify.ts) with a production spawnFn+clock; the CLI wrapper owns all printing and exit-code mapping. Extend parseIssueArgs (index.ts) with {mode:'close';id} / {mode:'abandon';id} positional branches (mirroring the existing `list` subcommand) and add matching in-process branches in dispatchIssue that print a human printHint line AND a machine `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>` (success) / `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR` (failure) line, exit 0 on result.ok else 1. Add a symmetric already-closed idempotency guard to closeIssueOnMain (abandon already has one). Update ISSUE_HELP to document both subcommands. In scope: parse + dispatch wiring, the one guard addition, help text, tests. OUT of scope: retrofitting the machine line onto `--file-local`/`list` (separate follow-up), any slash-command `/cam-issue close` form (CLI-only, no LLM), reason/comment arguments, warning when closing an issue others are blockedBy.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1: `cam issue close <id>` on an open, non-shipped issue sets stage:shipped on main via the existing commit-tree path (working branch untouched), prints a human hint plus a machine line `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>`, and exits 0. Oracle: named-command/integration test driving dispatchIssue mode:'close' (real or injected spawnFn) asserting the mutated CAM-NNNN.json on main, the printed CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id> line, and exit 0.

AC2: `cam issue abandon <id>` on an open issue sets status:abandoned on main (stage untouched), prints a hint plus `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>`, and exits 0. Oracle: integration test asserting status:abandoned on main, the line, exit 0.

AC3: `cam issue close <id>` on an ALREADY stage:shipped issue returns reason 'already-closed', prints `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR` plus the reason, and exits non-zero. Requires extending CloseIssueOnMainError (src/commands/issue-specify.ts:508-510) with 'already-closed' and adding a guard keyed STRICTLY on entry.stage === 'shipped' (never `!== 'specified'`). Oracle: unit test on closeIssueOnMain with a stage:'shipped' fixture asserting {ok:false, reason:'already-closed'}, plus a dispatch test asserting CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR + exit 1.

AC4: `cam issue abandon <id>` on an already-abandoned issue surfaces the existing 'already-abandoned' guard as `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR` and exit non-zero. Oracle: dispatch test with a status:'abandoned' fixture.

AC5: `cam issue close <id>` and `cam issue abandon <id>` on a not-found id print `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR` and exit non-zero (not-found reason). Oracle: dispatch test with an id absent from the backlog.

AC6: parseIssueArgs parses `close <id>` and `abandon <id>` as positional subcommands returning {mode:'close',id} / {mode:'abandon',id}; a missing id yields a parse error or help (never a silent text-mode fallthrough treating 'close'/'abandon' as an issue title). Oracle: unit test on parseIssueArgs in test/issue-dispatch.test.ts.

AC7: The close/abandon branches in dispatchIssue are in-process only and NEVER fall through to the runIssue thin-proxy (no tmux send-keys). Oracle: dispatch test mirroring the existing --file-local/list invariant that asserts the thin-proxy send-keys path is not invoked.
AC8: ISSUE_HELP documents `close <id>` and `abandon <id>`; `cam issue --help` renders them. Oracle: substring assertion on the help output.

AC9 (regression): The two existing callers of closeIssueOnMain (src/release/ship-pr.ts:150, src/release/post-merge.ts:323) keep passing their suites unchanged; the new already-closed error is tolerated by both (warning/error line, overall runShipPrStep/runPostMerge ok:true). Oracle: test/release/ship-pr.test.ts and test/release/post-merge.test.ts stay green.
AC10: `bun run check:all` (the full CI gate spine: typecheck, tests, embed-vendor, biome, ratchets, ci-parity) is green. Oracle: named-command exitCode 0.
gotchas: closeIssueOnMain is SHARED with the ship path (src/release/ship-pr.ts:150 and src/release/post-merge.ts:323). Both already inspect result.ok and tolerate a failed close as non-fatal narration (emitWarning/printError only, overall ok:true) -- verified SAFE via Explore, no existing test asserts an already-shipped close SUCCEEDS. The new guard MUST key strictly on entry.stage === 'shipped'; keying on `!== 'specified'` would wrongly error the AC1 fixture (stage:'specified') in test/issue-specify.test.ts.

close and abandon are on ORTHOGONAL axes (src/issues/types.ts): close sets stage:'shipped' (leaves status), abandon sets status:'abandoned' (leaves stage). IssueStage=idea|specified|planned|shipped; IssueStatus=open|abandoned. Do not conflate; an abandoned issue keeps its original stage.

closeIssueOnMain / abandonIssueOnMain are PURE return-only (no printing; they only printError inside shared guards on failure). The CLI wrapper (dispatchIssue branch) owns ALL printing (hint + CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line) and exit-code mapping. Mirror the existing dispatchIssue file-local branch (index.ts:1372-1414) for the pattern: parse -> in-process call -> map result.ok to exit 0/1.

DELIBERATE inconsistency: sibling deterministic paths (`--file-local`, `list`) print only printHint + exit code with NO CAM_ISSUE_* line. This issue intentionally ADDS `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>`/`=ERROR` (the sole existing shape, currently only inside the embedded LLM slash prompt src/vendor/_generated.ts) because close/abandon mutate backlog state mid-session and are exactly what the orchestrator wants to parse deterministically (the CAM-197 structured-handback thesis). Retrofitting the machine line onto --file-local/list is a SEPARATE tracked follow-up, not this issue.

Two test files share the name issue-specify.test.ts: closeIssueOnMain coverage is in test/issue-specify.test.ts (top-level), abandonIssueOnMain in test/commands/issue-specify.test.ts. New parse+dispatch tests belong in test/issue-dispatch.test.ts (already exercises parseIssueArgs + dispatchIssue routing invariants for --file-local/list).

clock and writeFile are declared-but-unused holdovers in CloseIssueOnMainOptions/AbandonIssueOnMainOptions (interface-compat post commit-tree cutover) but still required by the type; pass real ones anyway. _buildCreateIssueOpts (index.ts:1332-1355) is the reference for building a production spawnFn (spawnSync wrapped with stdio:'pipe') + clock: () => new Date().toISOString().

parseIssueArgs (index.ts:671-731) order is: --help first, then positional `list`, then `--file-local` flag, then free-text title fallthrough. Add `close`/`abandon` positional branches at the TOP alongside `list` so the id (args[1]) is consumed before the free-text branch can mistake 'close'/'abandon' for a title.
domainTerms: close (issue): the deterministic on-main mutation setting stage:shipped; models 'done/shipped', including an issue subsumed by another issue that shipped (e.g. CAM-192/198/180 subsumed by CAM-201).
abandon (issue): the deterministic on-main mutation setting status:abandoned; models 'won't-do / dropped'. Orthogonal to close.
Layer-1 CLI-exposure: a CAM-197-class change that wires an already-implemented on-main mutation function to a deterministic CLI subcommand with zero LLM in the path.

structured handback line: a machine-parseable stdout line (CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id> / CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR) a deterministic cam CLI emits so the orchestrator parses the outcome from stdout instead of reading the pane.
